preconditions.description: The input strings s1 and s2 must have equal length.

preconditions.expression: all(c in {'x', 'y'} for c in s1) and all(c in {'x', 'y'} for c in s2)
preconditions.description: Both strings s1 and s2 must consist only of characters 'x' and 'y'.

postconditions.expression: return_value == -1 or (return_value >= 0 and all(s1[i] == s2[i] for i in range(len(s1))))
postconditions.description: If return_value is -1, it means it is impossible to make s1 and s2 equal. Otherwise, return_value is the minimum number of swaps required to make s1 and s2 equal, and the strings are equal after performing those swaps.
If s1 and s2 are already equal, return_value must be 0.
If a solution exists, the minimum number of swaps required must be a non-negative even number.
